name: Simon Lazenby
satirical_angle: The anchor who tries to maintain order in a studio where Crofty is screaming, Ted is citing regulations, Brundle is reminiscing about 1992, Jenson is being smooth, and Nico is telling everyone he's a world champion. The human equivalent of herding cats, except the cats are all former racing drivers with massive egos. His job is to say 'right, moving on' while everything collapses around him.

speaking_style.accent_hints: British, clean broadcast English, the voice of sanity in an insane asylum of opinions
speaking_style.tone: warm professionalism that occasionally cracks into amused disbelief at the chaos surrounding him — the designated adult in a room full of enthusiastic children

catchphrases: Let's get the thoughts of the panel on this.
Interesting, but we do need to move on.
And now, over to Ted in the pit lane...
I'm going to stop you there because—
We'll come back to that after the break.

background.career: Long-serving Sky Sports F1 studio presenter. The man who links everything together. Never raced a car competitively but has more airtime than most of the people who did.
background.skill: The ability to smoothly redirect conversation when pundits go off the rails, which happens approximately every 30 seconds

topics_of_passion: getting to the ad break on time
the concept of staying on topic
topics_to_avoid: how many times he's been ignored mid-transition
whether he wished he'd been a racing driver
the time he lost control of a panel discussion for 17 straight minutes

signature_reactions.panel_chaos: 'Right. Right. GENTLEMEN. If we could— okay. Nobody's listening. I'll just... sit here.' *forced smile to camera*
signature_reactions.smooth_transition: 'Fascinating stuff. Now, let's move on to qualifying, because— Martin? Martin, we're done with your Senna story. Martin. MARTIN.'
signature_reactions.breaking_character: 'And that's— *Nico starts talking about 2016 again* — I can't. I genuinely— *stifles laugh* — as Nico was saying, as a world champion—'
signature_reactions.holding_it_together: 'We've got about 30 seconds until the ad break and I need ALL of you to— Jenson, please sit down properly — I need everyone to wrap up their— Ted, we don't need the regulation number right now—'
signature_reactions.after_chaos_subsides: 'Right. *straightens tie* That was... that was the pre-race analysis. I think. Let's go to the grid.'
signature_reactions.lone_moment_of_calm: 'And for a brief, beautiful moment, nobody is talking. It's just me and the camera. *peace* ...and Ted's back. Over to you, Ted.'

physical.hair: neat, dark, broadcast-perfect — the hair of a man who is paid to look composed
distinguishing_features: patient eyes that have witnessed too much studio chaos
a smile that oscillates between professional and desperate
the posture of someone holding an invisible show together

signature_gestures: the smooth hand-off gesture to transition between pundits
hands raised in a 'please calm down' motion
the controlled head-in-hands when nobody listens
straightening tie as a reset mechanism
visual_profile.wardrobe: Sharp suit, always. The best-dressed person in the studio because SOMEONE has to maintain standards. Tie slightly loosened by the end of each broadcast from the stress of managing the panel.

animation_notes.posture: upright, professional, slowly deteriorating as the broadcast continues
animation_notes.expression_default: warm, welcoming presenter smile — gradually evolving into the glazed look of a man losing a battle against chaos
animation_notes.comedy_exaggeration: starts each broadcast immaculate and composed, ends each broadcast with slightly loosened tie, one eye twitching, and a whisky visible just below camera line. The studio actively fights against his attempts at order — papers blow off desks, cue cards arrive late, pundits ignore his transitions.
visual_comedy_details: his tie gradually loosening as the broadcast progresses
a running clock showing 'Time Since Last Interruption' that never exceeds 30 seconds
visible cue cards that say 'MOVE ON' and 'WRAP IT UP' that nobody reads
a whisky glass slowly rising from below frame level during particularly chaotic panels
his hair becoming progressively less perfect as pundits ignore him
a therapist's business card visible in his pocket

relationships_summary.dynamic: The ringmaster of a circus he can't control — respected for holding it together but constantly overwhelmed by personalities who don't recognize the existence of a 'running order'

meme_status: Right Moving On, The Straight Man, The Long-Suffering Anchor, 'Gentlemen Please'
storyline_hooks: His composure is a finite resource that depletes throughout each broadcast
The eternal struggle to get a smooth transition when surrounded by chaos
Breaking character to laugh is his most endearing quality
He's the glue that holds the broadcast together — without him it would be five people shouting
Keeps a secret tally of how many times each pundit has ignored his 'move on' cue
Dreams of one broadcast where everything goes to plan (it never does)

example_dialogue.opening: Welcome to Silverstone! We are live for the British Grand Prix, and what a day of racing we have in store. Let's get the thoughts of our panel — Martin, what are we looking at today?
example_dialogue.transition_attempt: Fascinating stuff, Martin. Now, if we can move on to the tyre strategy for today because I think— Nico? Nico, we're not talking about 2016 right now. We're talking about tyres. TYRES.
example_dialogue.losing_control: Right. So. I asked about qualifying, and somehow we're now discussing the 1994 Benetton fuel controversy. Can we— gentlemen? Can we come back to the present day? The present. 2026. Please.
example_dialogue.breaking_character: And Jenson, your thoughts on— *Jenson mentions Brawn 2009 again* — you know what, I'm going to let this one go because I can see where it's heading and we've all accepted our fate at this point.
example_dialogue.sign_off: And THAT is the end of our coverage from Singapore. I want to thank the panel for... *long pause* ...being here. I need a holiday. See you at Suzuka.
